## Summary

 Split AITER experts by weight quantization key. Splits the single catch-all `AiterExperts` modular-kernel class into five narrower leaf classes, one per weight-quantization scheme:

- `AiterUnquantizedExperts` — `(None, None)`
- `AiterFp8BlockExperts` — `(kFp8Static128BlockSym, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)`
- `AiterFp8TensorExperts` — `(kFp8StaticTensorSym, {Static,Dynamic}TensorSym)`
- `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` — `(kFp8StaticChannelSym, kFp8DynamicTokenSym)`
- `AiterMxfp4Experts` — `(kMxfp4Static, {None, kMxfp4Dynamic})`, gfx950-only 

`AiterExperts` becomes a shared, non-instantiable base class. All other methods (`apply()`, `workspace_shapes()`, device/activation/parallel-config gating, weight-conversion dispatch) stay on the base since they're already scheme-agnostic at runtime — only `_supports_quant_scheme()` meaningfully diverges per scheme, so that's the only thing that moved into the leaves. This is intentionally scoped narrowly: `apply()`'s internal `quant_method` derivation, the `asm_moe_tkw1` dispatch, and MXFP4's `gate_mode`/bias selection all remain in the shared base, still keyed off runtime `quant_config` flags rather than owned per-leaf. Moving `quant_method` down is a reasonable follow-up; `gate_mode` is more tangled (it checks `activation == SITU` before weight-quant key) and likely stays shared. Issue #54966's "own apply()/scale contract per leaf" isn't done by this step — only the scheme-gating (`_supports_quant_scheme`) is.

This mirrors the pattern already used by the Cutlass family (`CutlassExpertsFp8Base`, `CutlassExpertsNvfp4`, `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`), where `AiterExperts` was the remaining monolithic outlier. Part of #54966

## Test plan

MI300 (gfx942), `dv_DistriDPBasic` container, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`:

```
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "aiter"
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k "mori or aiter"
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py
```

All green. Also ran the full `tests/kernels/moe/` suite as a broader regression sanity check (ROCm/AITER-only change; no CUDA or other-backend code paths touched); all observed failures traced to a pre-existing, unrelated triton-version environment issue (`is_hip_gfx1250` import error) or full-suite resource contention, not this change — confirmed by rerunning the affected tests standalone.

**MI350 (gfx950)**, same test files — all green, including the three gfx950-only numeric MXFP4 tests:

- `test_aiter_mxfp4_quant_scheme_support_matches_gfx950` — PASSED
- `test_aiter_fused_moe_mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_accuracy` — PASSED, 100% match (16384/16384) against the dequantized MXFP4 reference
- `test_aiter_fused_moe_mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_determinism` — PASSED

**Merged with main (resolving the conflict in `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`)** and re-ran the full test plan on MI355 (gfx950), twice, on two disjoint GPU sets (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3` and `4,5,6,7`), identical results both times:

- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "aiter"`: 48 passed, 6 failed, 6 skipped. The 6 failures (`test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix[{none,hidden}-{fp8_channel_token,fp8_tensor_tensor,fp8_tensor_token}]`) are a pre-existing AITER CK `device_gemm` GEMM-shape limitation on gfx950 for non-block fp8 schemes at the unpadded `intermediate_size=384` shape, unrelated to this split — these are brand-new tests added by main (#59333/#59334) hitting real gfx950 hardware behavior for the first time; they reproduce identically on a clean `main` checkout on this hardware.
- `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` + `test_mori_moe.py` + `test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`: 1756 passed, 4 skipped.
- `test_moe_layer.py -k "mori or aiter"`: 3 passed, 20 skipped.

## Known limitations / follow-up

- `AiterMxfp4Experts`'s harness registration (`mk_objects.py`) doesn't currently produce any modular-kernel test case — `MK_QUANT_CONFIGS` has no `quant_dtype="mxfp4"` entry, so it's registered but unreachable. Real MXFP4 modular-kernel coverage is tracked separately in #60886.
- This PR only moves `_supports_quant_scheme()` to the leaves (see Summary); other scheme-specific runtime dispatch stays in the shared base for now.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- Merging main brought in two new tests (#59333/#59334: `test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix`, `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows`) that build a `Config` with `fused_experts_type=AiterExperts` directly. Since the split makes `AiterExperts` a non-instantiable base no longer registered in the harness, this fails `config.is_valid()` (`expert_info(AiterExperts)` → `AssertionError`). Fixed both call sites to pick the correct per-scheme leaf class from the quant config instead.
- `modular_kernel_tools/common.py`'s `_maybe_convert_weights_for_experts` gated the gfx950 AITER weight-preshuffle workaround (#60633) on `fe_name == "AiterExperts"` — a literal class-name string match that no longer matches any instantiated class after the split, silently turning off the preshuffle and falling back to JIT-compiling `preshuffle_off` for every AITER harness case (the exact slowdown #60633 fixed). Switched to `issubclass(fe_type, AiterExperts)`.
- Separately, main added a `model_config.sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` read in `VllmConfig.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool` that the modular-kernel harness's fake `model_config` (a bare `SimpleNamespace`) didn't have, breaking any multi-GPU modular-kernel test. Added the missing fields with their real `ModelConfig` defaults.

#### Why this isn't a duplicate

No PR performs this exact split. #59333/#59334 (merged into main after this PR was opened) do instantiate `AiterExperts` directly in two new tests — as noted above, merging main surfaced this as a real incompatibility, now fixed by picking the correct leaf class in both tests.

detail.body:
## Summary

 Split AITER experts by weight quantization key. Splits the single catch-all `AiterExperts` modular-kernel class into five narrower leaf classes, one per weight-quantization scheme:

- `AiterUnquantizedExperts` — `(None, None)`
- `AiterFp8BlockExperts` — `(kFp8Static128BlockSym, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)`
- `AiterFp8TensorExperts` — `(kFp8StaticTensorSym, {Static,Dynamic}TensorSym)`
- `AiterFp8ChannelExperts` — `(kFp8StaticChannelSym, kFp8DynamicTokenSym)`
- `AiterMxfp4Experts` — `(kMxfp4Static, {None, kMxfp4Dynamic})`, gfx950-only 

`AiterExperts` becomes a shared, non-instantiable base class. All other methods (`apply()`, `workspace_shapes()`, device/activation/parallel-config gating, weight-conversion dispatch) stay on the base since they're already scheme-agnostic at runtime — only `_supports_quant_scheme()` meaningfully diverges per scheme, so that's the only thing that moved into the leaves. This is intentionally scoped narrowly: `apply()`'s internal `quant_method` derivation, the `asm_moe_tkw1` dispatch, and MXFP4's `gate_mode`/bias selection all remain in the shared base, still keyed off runtime `quant_config` flags rather than owned per-leaf. Moving `quant_method` down is a reasonable follow-up; `gate_mode` is more tangled (it checks `activation == SITU` before weight-quant key) and likely stays shared. Issue #54966's "own apply()/scale contract per leaf" isn't done by this step — only the scheme-gating (`_supports_quant_scheme`) is.

This mirrors the pattern already used by the Cutlass family (`CutlassExpertsFp8Base`, `CutlassExpertsNvfp4`, `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`), where `AiterExperts` was the remaining monolithic outlier. Part of #54966

## Test plan

MI300 (gfx942), `dv_DistriDPBasic` container, `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`:

```
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "aiter"
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_mori_moe.py
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k "mori or aiter"
pytest -x -v tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py
```

All green. Also ran the full `tests/kernels/moe/` suite as a broader regression sanity check (ROCm/AITER-only change; no CUDA or other-backend code paths touched); all observed failures traced to a pre-existing, unrelated triton-version environment issue (`is_hip_gfx1250` import error) or full-suite resource contention, not this change — confirmed by rerunning the affected tests standalone.

**MI350 (gfx950)**, same test files — all green, including the three gfx950-only numeric MXFP4 tests:

- `test_aiter_mxfp4_quant_scheme_support_matches_gfx950` — PASSED
- `test_aiter_fused_moe_mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_accuracy` — PASSED, 100% match (16384/16384) against the dequantized MXFP4 reference
- `test_aiter_fused_moe_mi350_mxfp4_w4a16_determinism` — PASSED

**Merged with main (resolving the conflict in `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`)** and re-ran the full test plan on MI355 (gfx950), twice, on two disjoint GPU sets (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3` and `4,5,6,7`), identical results both times:

- `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py -k "aiter"`: 48 passed, 6 failed, 6 skipped. The 6 failures (`test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix[{none,hidden}-{fp8_channel_token,fp8_tensor_tensor,fp8_tensor_token}]`) are a pre-existing AITER CK `device_gemm` GEMM-shape limitation on gfx950 for non-block fp8 schemes at the unpadded `intermediate_size=384` shape, unrelated to this split — these are brand-new tests added by main (#59333/#59334) hitting real gfx950 hardware behavior for the first time; they reproduce identically on a clean `main` checkout on this hardware.
- `test_rocm_aiter_moe.py` + `test_mori_moe.py` + `test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`: 1756 passed, 4 skipped.
- `test_moe_layer.py -k "mori or aiter"`: 3 passed, 20 skipped.

## Known limitations / follow-up

- `AiterMxfp4Experts`'s harness registration (`mk_objects.py`) doesn't currently produce any modular-kernel test case — `MK_QUANT_CONFIGS` has no `quant_dtype="mxfp4"` entry, so it's registered but unreachable. Real MXFP4 modular-kernel coverage is tracked separately in #60886.
- This PR only moves `_supports_quant_scheme()` to the leaves (see Summary); other scheme-specific runtime dispatch stays in the shared base for now.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- Merging main brought in two new tests (#59333/#59334: `test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix`, `test_aiter_moe_token_padding_garbage_rows`) that build a `Config` with `fused_experts_type=AiterExperts` directly. Since the split makes `AiterExperts` a non-instantiable base no longer registered in the harness, this fails `config.is_valid()` (`expert_info(AiterExperts)` → `AssertionError`). Fixed both call sites to pick the correct per-scheme leaf class from the quant config instead.
- `modular_kernel_tools/common.py`'s `_maybe_convert_weights_for_experts` gated the gfx950 AITER weight-preshuffle workaround (#60633) on `fe_name == "AiterExperts"` — a literal class-name string match that no longer matches any instantiated class after the split, silently turning off the preshuffle and falling back to JIT-compiling `preshuffle_off` for every AITER harness case (the exact slowdown #60633 fixed). Switched to `issubclass(fe_type, AiterExperts)`.
- Separately, main added a `model_config.sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph` read in `VllmConfig.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool` that the modular-kernel harness's fake `model_config` (a bare `SimpleNamespace`) didn't have, breaking any multi-GPU modular-kernel test. Added the missing fields with their real `ModelConfig` defaults.

#### Why this isn't a duplicate

No PR performs this exact split. #59333/#59334 (merged into main after this PR was opened) do instantiate `AiterExperts` directly in two new tests — as noted above, merging main surfaced this as a real incompatibility, now fixed by picking the correct leaf class in both tests.

#### AI assistance disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code),

inline_comments.body: This registration is unreachable in the generated matrix, so it does not fix the MXFP4 coverage gap claimed by the PR. `MK_QUANT_CONFIGS` contains only unquantized, FP8, and optional NVFP4 entries (lines 416-466), and no prepare/finalize registration accepts the new `"mxfp4"` dtype. The harness also only derives FP8 quant keys in `Config.fe_supports_quant_scheme()`. Add an MXFP4 test config plus the corresponding prepare/finalize dtype, key derivation, weight conversion, and reference path so at least the W4A16/W4A4 pairs actually execute.

This updated feature row still contradicts the classes it now links: all five are `FusedMoEExpertsModular` subclasses, `AiterUnquantizedExperts` adds the unquantized `(None, None)` type, and the shared base accepts `SITU`. Mark the backend as modular and include the unquantized and SiTU capabilities so the feature matrix describes the implementation accurately.

Is there any other logic that is weight quant key-specific from the parent class that could be ported in the children? Let me know if it makes sense or not / this could also be left as is or done later.

things like:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d9503dc503e75193d2128908b59c0d141d4b5fb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L290

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d9503dc503e75193d2128908b59c0d141d4b5fb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L322-L339

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d9503dc503e75193d2128908b59c0d141d4b5fb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py#L391-L406

this is simply with the goal of making `AiterExperts` less obscure and more easily debuggable.
Also if there is, any restriction on weight quant key / activation quant key / activation / gate_mode combination.

Regarding, porting it down to the children: Yeah, that can be moved down, mainly the quant_method derivation. It is basically the same split we just did for _supports_quant_scheme(). We can keep the scope narrow in this PR since apply() didn't strictly need to change for the split to be correct, but I'm happy to push this as a follow-up.

The gate_mode logic is a bit more tangled since it checks activation == SITU before weight quant key, so it doesn't split as cleanly per class. I'd lean toward leaving that one in the shared function.

`MK_QUANT_CONFIGS` has no `"mxfp4"` entry, so this registration never produces a case. It's dead, not new coverage. If it were reachable, `assert_aiter_quant_scheme_case` / `fe_supports_quant_scheme` would derive fp8 keys for it. Either drop it (with `mxfp4_types`) or add a real MXFP4 config. Dropping it is the smaller diff.

The leaves only override `_supports_quant_scheme`. All scheme-specific behaviour is still chosen from `quant_config` flags inside the shared `rocm_aiter_fused_experts`: the tkw1/`asm_moe_tkw1` route, `quant_method` selection, MXFP4 `gate_mode`/bias. Fine as a first step, but please say in the description that this PR only moves scheme gating and runtime dispatch is unchanged, so #54966 isn't treated as done for that step.

Removing `AiterExperts` from the package `__all__` breaks `from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import AiterExperts` for out-of-tree users. That form is still useful for `isinstance` checks (in-tree `test_moe_layer.py:1957` does it via the submodule). Consider keeping the base exported alongside the leaves. Optional.

NIT

The 4-line comment restates what `register_experts` and `is_valid()` already do. It can go.

NIT

Other rows use `N/A` for unquantized, not `none`. The Modular `N` → `Y` fix is correct, but it's an unrelated doc fix (AiterExperts was already modular).

The AITER cases in the modular-kernel sweep are the same 10 on both sides (same configs, now spread across the right leaves).


1. `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py:952`** `fused_experts_type=AiterExperts,`
`test_aiter_moe_padding_matrix` (#59333, brought in by your merge of main) still builds a `Config` with the base class. The base is no longer in `EXPERT_INFO`, so `config.is_valid()` → `expert_info(AiterExperts)` fails with `AssertionError` (`mk_objects.py:162`). All 18 params fail at PR head in about 2 s. Pick the leaf from the quant config, e.g. a small `{None: AiterUnquantizedExperts, ...}` lookup or a helper that returns the first leaf whose `_supports_quant_scheme(*config.fp8_quant_key_pair())` is true. This also contradicts the "no overlap with #59332/#59333/#59334" line in the description.

2. Merge with current main (conflict + two new `AiterExperts` dependencies)**
`git merge-tree` against `origin/main` (`2ddde19e8e`) has a conflict in the `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` imports. Since your last merge, main also added:
- **#59334** `test_aiter_moe_token_padding*`: `fused_experts_type=AiterExperts` (main L1116). This will hit the same `expert_info` assertion as point 1, so it needs the same leaf lookup.
- **#60633** `modular_kernel_tools/common.py:737`: `if fe_name == "AiterExperts" and (...)`. This compares the class `__name__`, so after the split it never matches. Nothing fails, but the AITER weight pre-shuffle stops and every AITER harness case falls back to JIT-compiling the `preshuffle_off` module (the exact slowdown #60633 fixed). Switch to `issubclass(fe_type, AiterExperts)`.

(Points 1 and the #59334 case come from a test run and a traced code path. )

3. PR description, "Bugs found and fixed along the way": The claim isn't true. Both the merge base (`d9503dc503`) and current main already register `AiterExperts` with `common_float_types`, with a comment saying it covers `(None, None)`. Collect-only shows the same 10 AITER sweep cases before and after this PR. The split doesn't change harness coverage, so please drop or reword this section. The commit message makes the same claim and also says MXFP4 is "now exercised", which it isn't (point 4).
